summary: Luca Maria Olivieri is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology who earned his doctorate from Freie Universität Berlin (attested 2010). He directed the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East and became an associate professor at Ca' Foscari University of Venice around 2020.

Lucia Dolce works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She held lecturer and associate professor posts at SOAS University of London (attested 2003–2015) and is attested as a guest researcher at Minobusan University in 2026.
Lucia Galli is a scholar of Tibetology who completed her doctorate at the University of Oxford and held a post there.

Lucian Scherman was an Indologist who studied at Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and at Munich under Ernst Kuhn. He served as a curator and director at the Museum Fünf Kontinente and was a professor at the University of Munich (~1893–1936).

Luciano Petech was a scholar of Tibetology, history, archaeology, and Sinology who studied under Giuseppe Tucci. He taught at Allahabad (1938–1946) and held the Chair of History of Eastern Asia at Sapienza University of Rome (1955–1984).

Lucien Lévy-Bruhl was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who studied at the École Normale Supérieure and the Sorbonne. He founded the Institut d'Ethnologie and served on the faculty at the University of Paris (~1899–1927).

Lucien Tesnière was a linguist who studied at the University of Paris, Leipzig, ENLOV, and under Antoine Meillet. He held academic posts at the University of Ljubljana (~1924–1937), University of Strasbourg (1924–1937), and University of Montpellier (1937).
Lucy Annette Jones is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who completed her PhD at Rice University under the supervision of Anne C. Klein and Edith Wyschogrod.

Ludo Rocher was an Indologist who earned law degrees and a PhD at Ghent University, also studying under Adriaan Scharpé and Jan Gonda. He taught at Université libre de Bruxelles (1959–1967) before serving as a professor at the University of Pennsylvania (1966–2002).

Ludwig Alsdorf was an Indologist who studied under Walther Schubring at Hamburg and Heinrich Lüders at Berlin. He taught at the University of Allahabad (1930–1932), Humboldt University of Berlin (1935, 1944), and held a chair at Hamburg (1950–1972).

Ludwig Diestel was a religious studies scholar who studied under Heinrich Ewald. He held posts at the universities of Bonn (~1858–1862), Greifswald (~1862–1867), Jena (~1867–1874), and Tübingen (~1874–1879).

Ludwig Heller was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Göttingen under Franz Kielhorn and completed his habilitation at Greifswald. He served as an associate professor at the University of Greifswald (1904) and held a post at the University of Tartu (1918).

Ludwig Lange was a scholar in linguistics and history who studied at Leipzig and Göttingen under Theodor Benfey. He served as a professor of classical philology at Charles University (1853–1859), University of Giessen (1859), and University of Leipzig (1871–1880).

Ludwig Ross was a history and archaeology scholar who studied at Kiel University (~1825–1829). He held academic posts at the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens (1837–1843) and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1845–1859).
Ludwig Timotheus Spittler was a historian who studied at the University of Tübingen (~1771–1775) and served on the faculty at the University of Göttingen (~1779–1797).

Ludwig Wittgenstein was a philosopher who studied at TU Berlin, Manchester, and Cambridge, where he earned his PhD. He spent his academic career at Cambridge, serving as a fellow and lecturer at Trinity College and as professor of philosophy (1930–1947).
Ludwik Skurzak was an Indologist who studied under Stanisław Schayer and served as a lecturer at the University of Breslau.
Luigi Suali was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at the University of Bologna and under Hermann Jacobi. He held a post at the University of Pavia from around 1907 to 1951.

Luis O. Gómez was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at Yale under Stanley Insler. He held long-term professorships and chair roles at the University of Michigan and served as academic director at the Mangalam Research Center (~2010–2017).

Luise Hercus was an Indologist and linguist educated at St Anne's College, Oxford, and the Australian National University. She tutored at St Anne's (1948–1954) and lectured in Sanskrit at the Australian National University (~1969–1991).
